text:
alex: Quick sync — we need to decide if the SDKs should treat pagination cursors as completely opaque strings or expose a small structured view for retries/idempotency.
priya: my vote: opaque. less surface area, fewer compatibility promises.
josh: opaque is safer, but we lose the ability to do smart client-side retries (e.g. resume after partial page).
maria: what's the concrete problem with opaque + server-assisted resume?
alex: example: user fetches page with cursor `c1`. network blips after processing page N, client retries and gets duplicate items without a way to dedupe. If cursor is opaque, client can't tell where to resume, needs server to support idempotent replays or server-provided resume hints.
priya: we already have server-side resume hints in some endpoints (header: `x-resume-hint`). can we standardize that header instead of exposing structured cursor?
josh: header helps but is extra round-trip info. For high-throughput SDKs (python/ts/go) ergonomics matter — we want a simple `iterator.resume()` without forcing users to manage tokens manually.
maria: what about a hybrid: cursor stays opaque, but SDKs can parse a small base64-encoded metadata suffix we control (like `opaque::base64({"seq":123,"shard":2})`). server can ignore unknown suffixes. SDKs can optionally decode it for retry heuristics.
alex: that reduces server contract surface, but it leaks some structure. concerns about coupling and security (leak internal shard IDs).
priya: security-wise we can HMAC the metadata so clients can't tamper. server verifies on resume. still privacy concerns.
josh: also language SDKs would need shared util to decode and verify HMAC. adds maintenance.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: staging rollout 2.1.3 includes `x-resume-hint` feature flag for 10% canaries.
maria: alternative: keep cursor opaque, but add an optional `retry_token` that is a short-lived idempotency handle returned at page fetch time. clients include `retry_token` when retrying; server uses it to dedupe. lightweight and explicit.
alex: I like `retry_token`. fits our existing idempotency patterns for writes. Makes retries explicit rather than implicit interpretation of cursor.
priya: cost: server needs to store retry tokens briefly or check in cache. memory tradeoff.
josh: that's ok; we already have short-lived caches for uploads/requests. implementing in runtime should be straightforward.
maria: UX: SDKs expose `next_page(retry_token=...)` under the hood. iterator auto-passes the last `retry_token` when retrying network errors. no API break for users.
alex: cross-language surfaces: Python/TS/Go SDKs should implement the auto-retry-with-retry_token behavior, but provide an opt-out flag `auto_resume_on_retries: bool` default true.
priya: docs: add a snippet showing how to opt-out and manually manage `retry_token` if people want custom dedupe.
josh: streaming endpoints? we still need a plan for long-lived streams. `retry_token` model doesn't map perfectly. but for paginated HTTP it's solid.
maria: for streams, keep existing resume tokens (opaque) and push a follow-up RFC for stream resume semantics.
alex: decision summary so far: 1) Keep cursors opaque. 2) Add optional short-lived `retry_token` on paginated responses for client-side safe retries. 3) SDKs auto-use `retry_token` to dedupe retry responses; expose `auto_resume_on_retries` toggle. 4) Standardize optional header `x-retry-token` / `x-resume-hint` as fallbacks. 5) Follow-up RFC for stream resume.
priya: agreed. I'll open a tiny PR to add `retry_token` header to the runtime and update the console docs.
josh: I'll sketch SDK changes: python iterator will catch network errors, call `next_page(retry_token=last_retry_token)`, and surface an `IteratorResumeError` when the server can't reconcile.
maria: can we add a lightweight test harness? CI-bot: suggest adding a flaky-network integration test toggled by env var.
ci-bot: note: create integration test in `eng-platform/pagination-tests` that toggles `RETRY_TOKEN_ENABLED`.
alex: timeline: Priya + Josh to land runtime + python/ts SDK changes in two sprints. Maria will handle docs and tests. I'll file the follow-up RFC for streams.
priya: tagging @josh for the SDK ergonomics sketch.
josh: on it, will DM if I need details.
maria: thanks all. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: prod-monitor: watch pagination-error-rate for next 72h after rollout.
alex: ok closing thread — I'll update the RFC issue with the decision note and link to PRs.
